'''Kim Jae Kyoung''' ({{Korean|hangul=김재경}}; born December 14, 1982) is a biomedical mathematician and associate professor at [[KAIST]] in the Department of Mathematical Sciences<ref>{{cite web |url=https://horizon.kias.re.kr/author/%EA%B9%80%EC%9E%AC%EA%B2%BD |script-title=ko:김재경: KAIST 수리과학과 부교수 |author= <!--Not stated--> |date= |website= Horizon |publisher= [[Korea Institute for Advanced Study]]  |access-date= 11 January 2024 |quote= |language= Korean}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url= http://events.kias.re.kr/h/HCMCPL/?pageNo=5209 |script-title=ko:고등과학원 허준이 수학난제연구소 대중강연 시리즈 |author= <!--Not stated--> |date= |website= [[Korea Institute for Advanced Study]] |publisher= |access-date= 11 January 2024 |quote= |language= Korean}}</ref> and a chief investigator in the Pioneer Research Center for Mathematical and Computational Sciences at the [[Institute for Basic Science]]. His research focuses on [[mathematical and theoretical biology|mathematical biology]] and [[medicine]], specifically the combination of nonlinear dynamics, the theory of [[stochastic process]]es, and [[computational science]], to better understand disease mechanisms and develop relevant treatment strategies, including drug and digital medicine for sleep disorders.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.ibs.re.kr/cop/bbs/BBSMSTR_000000000739/selectBoardArticle.do?nttId=19753&pageIndex=1&searchCnd=&searchWrd= |title= A New IBS Center in Mathematical Biology Kicks Off |author=<!--Not stated--> |date= 11 March 2021 |website= [[Institute for Basic Science]] |publisher= |access-date= 19 March 2021 |quote= }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url= https://ithems.riken.jp/en/news/ithems-biology-seminar-dr-jae-kyoung-kim-november-11-2021 |title= iTHEMS Biology Seminar by Dr. Jae Kyoung Kim on November 11, 2021 |author= Gen Kurosawa |date= 17 November 2021 |website= Interdisciplinary Theoretical and Mathematical Sciences Program |publisher= [[RIKEN]] |access-date= 11 January 2024 |quote=}}</ref>

==Education==
Kim was born in [[Daegu]], South Korea in 1982. He attended Yeungnam Middle School and [[Yeungnam High School]] before moving to Seoul where he graduated [[summa cum laude]] with a B.A. in mathematics education from [[Seoul National University]] in 2005. Reading a news article about using math to study heart disease led him to the [[University of Michigan]] as it was known for mathematical biology.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://m.dongascience.com/news.php?idx=47673 |script-title=ko:[주말N수학] 생명의 비밀 파헤치는 수학의 세계 |author= <!--Not stated--> |date= 10 July 2021 |website= [[Donga Science]] |publisher= |access-date= 17 January 2024 |quote= |language= Korean}}</ref> He received his Ph.D. in applied and interdisciplinary mathematics in 2013. He received the [[Sumner Byron Myers]] Prize for this thesis on cellular clocks.<ref name=":byron">{{cite web |url=https://lsa.umich.edu/math/graduates/StudentAwards/department-awards.html |title=Department Awards |author= <!--Not stated--> |date= |website= LSA Mathematics |publisher= University of Michigan |access-date= 29 August 2022 |quote= |language= }}</ref><ref name=":byron2">{{cite web |url=https://lsa.umich.edu/content/dam/math-assets/math-document/continuum/2014%20ContinuUM.pdf |title=ContinuUM |author= <!--Not stated--> |date=2014 |website= Department of Mathematics |publisher= University of Michigan |access-date= 29 September 2022 |quote= }}</ref> His advisors were Daniel Forger and Victoria Booth while [[Trachette Jackson]] was a thesis committee member.

==Career==
Kim was a postdoctoral fellow at the [[Mathematical Biosciences Institute]] within [[Ohio State University]].<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.math.utah.edu/research/mathbio/mbseminar/mathbio_seminar_spring_2015.html |title= Weekly Mathematical Biology Seminar |author= <!--Not stated--> |date= 2015 |website= Department of Mathematics |publisher= University of Utah |access-date= 29 August 2022 |quote= |language= }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.math.fsu.edu/~mio/courses/biomath14/kim.math |title= Biomathematics Seminar |author= <!--Not stated--> |date= |website=Department of Mathematics |publisher= Florida State University |access-date= 29 August 2022 |quote= |language= }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www-personal.umich.edu/~forger/forgertenurecv.pdf |title= Daniel B. Forger III |author= <!--Not stated--> |date= |website= University of Michigan |publisher= |access-date= 29 August 2022 |quote= |language= }}</ref> Returning to Korea, he served as an assistant<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/468086 |title= KAIST's mathematician reveals the mechanism for sustaining biological rhythms |author= <!--Not stated--> |date= 28 August 2015 |website= [[American Association for the Advancement of Science#EurekAlert!]] |publisher= |access-date= 11 January 2024 |quote= }}</ref> and associate professor in the Department of Mathematical Science in [[KAIST]].<ref>{{cite web |url= https://mathsci.kaist.ac.kr/home/2021/11/%ec%88%98%eb%a6%ac%ea%b3%bc%ed%95%99%ea%b3%bc-%ea%b9%80%ec%9e%ac%ea%b2%bd-%ea%b5%90%ec%88%98-%ec%98%ac%ed%95%b4%ec%9d%98-%ec%b5%9c%ec%84%9d%ec%a0%95%ec%83%81-%ec%88%98%ec%83%81%e2%80%8b |script-title=ko:김재경 교수, 올해의 최석정상 수상|author= <!--Not stated--> |date= 30 November 2021 |website= Department of Mathematical Sciences |publisher= [[KAIST]] |access-date= 11 January 2024 |quote= |language= Korean}}</ref> He also worked as an associate member at the [[Korea Institute for Advanced Study]] from 2018 and then as a visiting scholar in the Department of Mathematics in the University of Michigan from 2019 to 2020. He became a member of Young Korean Academy of Science and Technology in 2019.<ref name=":young"/>

In March 2021, Kim became a chief investigator of the Pioneer Research Center for Mathematical and Computational Sciences at the Institute for Basic Science (IBS), heading the Biomedical Mathematics Group (BIMAG).<ref>{{cite web |url= https://science.ytn.co.kr/program/program_view.php?s_mcd=0082&s_hcd=&key=202102261629466984 |title= IBS 수리·계산과학연구단 의생명 수학 그룹 출범 |author= 최소라 |date= 26 February 2021  |website= YTN Science |publisher= [[YTN]] |access-date= 19 March 2021 |quote= |language= Korean}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.dongascience.com/news.php?idx=44318 |script-title=ko:생물학 난제 수학적 관점에서 푼다…IBS 신규연구그룹 출범 |author= 고재원 |date= 26 February 2021 |website= |publisher= [[Donga Science]] |access-date= 17 January 2024 |quote= |language= Korean}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://news.heraldcorp.com/view.php?ud=20210226000166 |script-title=ko:수리생물학으로 수면질환 치료법 찾는다…IBS '의생명 수학그룹' 출범 |author= <!--Not stated--> |date= 26 February 2021 |website= |publisher= [[Herald Corporation]] |access-date= 17 January 2024 |quote= |language= Korean}}</ref> Three teams conduct research at BIMAG. The Intracellular Dynamics Team develops reduction methods for multi-scale stochastic systems and identifies molecular mechanisms underlying robust circadian rhythms. The Intercellular Dynamics Team develops inference methods for dynamic networks and causes of and treatment strategies for circadian rhythm sleep disorders at the network level. The Systemic Dynamics Team develops methods for analyzing noisy human activity data from wearable devices and their application to identify optimal sleep patterns, and develops chronotherapy for sleep disorders and cancer.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.ibs.re.kr/bimag/research-aim |title= Research Aim |author= <!--Not stated--> |date= |website= IBS Biomedical Mathematics Group |publisher= [[Institute for Basic Science]] |access-date= 11 January 2024 |quote= }}</ref>

===Mechanisms for period regulation of circadian clock===
Despite temperature changes, Kim found a mathematical model which underlies a molecular mechanism for regulation of the [[circadian clock]]. This biological clock was discovered in 1954, but the method for how it operates took more than 60 years to understand. Relevant factors include the topology of biochemical network underlying the circadian clock, phospho-switch that controls stability of key repressor proteins can compensate the effects of temperature, cells in the mammalian circadian clocks are coupled to generate synchronized rhythms, and a mechanism that filters [[stochastic]]ity in the circadian clock.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.donga.com/en/article/all/20151006/411572/1 |title=Korean researcher solves 60-year-old puzzle of biological clock through math |author= <!--Not stated--> |date= 6 October 2015 |website= [[The Dong-A Ilbo]] |publisher= |access-date= 17 January 2024 |quote= |language= }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url= https://news.kaist.ac.kr/newsen/html/news/?mode=V&mng_no=4822&skey=department&sval=Department+of+Mathematical+science&list_s_date=&list_e_date=&GotoPage=1 |title= Professor Jae Kyoung Kim Receives the 2017 HSFP Award |author= <!--Not stated--> |date= 21 July 2017 |website= [[KAIST]] |publisher= |access-date= 30 November 2023 |quote= }}</ref>

===Mathematical models to treat diseases caused by disrupted circadian rhythms===
Misalignment of [[circadian rhythm]]s with the external environment can cause significant physiological problems. Kim studied the drug [[Casein kinase 1 isoform epsilon#PF-670462 and PF-4800567|PF-670462]] which aims to realign the circadian clock. Using [[Pharmacokinetics|pharmacokinetic data]], he built a pharmacology model and analyzed the phase response curve to the drug and light which helped to predict the drug's effect under various environmental conditions.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.kaist.ac.kr/newsen/html/news/?mode=V&mng_no=12930&skey=department&sval=Department+of+Mathematical+Sciences&list_s_date=&list_e_date=&GotoPage=1 |title= Professor Jae Kyoung Kim to Lead a New Mathematical Biology Research Group at IBS |author= <!--Not stated--> |date= 18 March 2021 |website= News |publisher= [[KAIST]] |access-date= 17 January 2024 |quote= |language= }}</ref> As disruption of circadian rhythms increases the risk of getting cancer, he studied the interactions between [[p53]] and [[PER2]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Gotoh |first1=Tetsuya  |last2=Kim  |first2=Jae Kyoung  |last3=Liu |first3= Jingjing |last4= Finkielstein |first4=Carla V. |date= 9 November 2016 |title= Model-driven experimental approach reveals the complex regulatory distribution of p53 by the circadian factor Period 2 |journal= [[PNAS]] |volume= 113|issue= 47|pages=3516–13521 |doi= 10.1073/pnas.1607984113|doi-access=free |pmid=27834218 |pmc=5127372 |bibcode=2016PNAS..11313516G }}</ref>

===Derivation of validity condition for stochastic QSSA===
Kim was the first to propose and then prove multiple results in justifying the stochastic [[Steady state (chemistry)|quasi-steady state approximation]] (QSSA).<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kim |first1=Jae Kyoung  |last2= Josic|first2=Kresimir |last3=Bennett |first3= Matthew R. |date=5 August 2014  |title=The Validity of Quasi-Steady-State Approximations in Discrete Stochastic Simulations |journal= Biophysical Journal |volume= 107 |issue= 3|pages= 783–793 |doi= 10.1016/j.bpj.2014.06.012|pmid=25099817 |pmc=4129492 |arxiv=1406.2244 |bibcode=2014BpJ...107..783K }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kim |first1=Jae Kyoung  |last2=Josić |first2=Krešimir  |last3=Bennett |first3= Matthew R. |date=23 November 2015 |title=The relationship between stochastic and deterministic quasi-steady state approximations |journal= BMC Systems Biology |volume= 9 |issue= |page=87 |doi= 10.1186/s12918-015-0218-3|doi-access=free |pmid=26597159 |pmc=4657384 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1= Kim|first1=Jae Kyoung  |last2=Rempala |first2=Grzegorz  |last3= Kang|first3=Hye-Won |author-link2= Grzegorz Rempala |date=12 October 2017 |title=Reduction for Stochastic Biochemical Reaction Networks with Multiscale Conservations |journal= Multiscale Modeling & Simulation |volume=15 |issue= 4 |pages=1376–1403 |doi=10.1137/16M1099443 |arxiv=1704.05628 |s2cid=7497139 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kim |first1=Jae Kyoung |last2=Sontag |first2=Eduardo D.  |author-link2= Eduardo D. Sontag |date=5 June 2017 |title= Reduction of multiscale stochastic biochemical reaction networks using exact moment derivation|journal=PLOS Computational Biology |volume=13 |issue=6 |article-number= e1005571 |doi= 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1005571|doi-access=free |pmid=28582397 |pmc=5481150 |bibcode=2017PLSCB..13E5571K }}</ref><ref name="Universally valid reduction of mult">{{cite journal |last1=Song |first1= Yun Min |last2=Hong |first2=Hyukpyo  |last3=Kim |first3= Jae Kyoung |date= 18 October 2018 |title= Universally valid reduction of multiscale stochastic biochemical systems using simple non-elementary propensities |journal= [[PLOS Computational Biology]] |volume= 17|issue= 10|article-number= e1008952|doi=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008952 |doi-access= free |pmid= 34662330 |pmc= 8562860 }}</ref>
The approximation has been widely used to reduce stochastic model of various biological systems.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://ww2.amstat.org/meetings/jsm/2018/onlineprogram/AbstractDetails.cfm?abstractid=328960 |title= An Estimation Method for Enzyme Kinetic Model Parameters Based on Bayesian Approach |author= <!--Not stated--> |date=31 July 2018 |website= JSM 2018 |publisher= [[American Statistical Association]] |access-date= 6 February 2024 |quote= |language= }}</ref> Despite its common use, there has been a critical problem in understanding whether the stochastic QSSA is accurate and under what conditions it may fail. Kim has worked to developing a method to compute the error of the stochastic QSSA directly. This provided a clear guideline for when and how to use the stochastic QSSA. Furthermore, he developed a new method for simplifying models when the stochastic QSSA is invalid.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.kms.or.kr/conference/abstract/search_view.html?num=8331&uid=82&start=0&sort=sortDate&period=82&cate=&etitle=&key_word=&au_name=&au_ename=&au_office=&au_eoffice=&mode=&section= |title= The relationship between deterministic and stochastic quasi-steady-state approximations. |author= <!--Not stated--> |date= |website= [[Korean Mathematical Society]] |publisher= |access-date= 6 February 2024 |quote= |language= }}</ref><ref name="Universally valid reduction of mult"/>

===Discovering and correcting the error in the equation of FDA guidelines===
Kim found errors in the US [[Food and Drug Administration]]'s (FDA) current guidance for predicting how [[drug interaction|drugs interact in the body]] and created a more accurate formula. The current FDA method is inaccurate, requiring artificial adjustments. The new formula is based on an improved mathematical foundation and can accurately predict drug metabolism rates without artificial factors. When tested, the new formula predicted drug interactions accurately 80% of the time compared to 38% with the equation in FDA guidance. This improvement could greatly enhance drug development and safety in clinical use.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://news.kaist.ac.kr/newsen/html/news/?mode=V&mng_no=26490 |title=Scientists re-writes FDA-recommended equation to improve estimation of drug-drug interaction |author= <!--Not stated--> |date=18 January 2023 |website= |publisher= [[KAIST]] |access-date= 29 January 2024 |quote= |language= }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url= https://news.heraldcorp.com/view.php?ud=20230111000418 |script-title=ko:[헤럴드광장] 수학이 생명에 필요한 순간 |author= Kim Jae Kyoung |date= 11 January 2023 |website= |publisher= [[Herald Corporation]] |access-date= 29 January 2024 |quote= |language= Korean}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url= https://news.heraldcorp.com/view.php?ud=20230104000312 |title= "美 FDA보다 더 정확" 韓 연구진, 약물 상호작용 예측 수식 개발 |author= <!--Not stated--> |date= 4 January 2023 |website= 헤럴드경제 |publisher= |access-date= 6 February 2024 |quote= |language= Korean}}</ref>

===Software development===
BIMAG has also made various software during their research, including mathematical models for [[oscillation#Biological|biological oscillators]], [[Bayesian inference|Bayesian inference algorithms]], [[stochastic calculus|stochastic analysis]], [[causal inference|causality inference]], diagnosis for [[sleep disorder]]s, and [[sleep tracking|sleep data imputation]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ibs.re.kr/bimag/software |title= Software |author= <!--Not stated--> |date= |website= IBS Biomedical Mathematics Group |publisher= [[Institute for Basic Science]] |access-date= 11 January 2024 |quote= }}</ref>
